title: Momentum Contrastive Learning (MoCo)
reading: The slide introduces MoCo as a contrastive self-supervised method whose objective is to maximize similarity between positive pairs while minimizing similarity between negative pairs. A pipeline sketch accompanies the bullets, showing a query image and a key image each passed through their own encoder before a contrastive loss is computed; the text notes that the query encoder is updated directly while the key encoder is updated by a moving average.

visuals.description: Two-branch pipeline: a query image and a key image each feed into an encoder; outputs meet at a loss node. Annotations indicate 'Update encoder q' and 'Update encoder k by moving average'.
visuals.assertion: MoCo uses asymmetric encoders — the query encoder is trained by gradients while the key encoder is a momentum (moving-average) copy.
